questions.scenarioContext: An end-user receives an email requesting access to the IT system in exchange for a service to improve network speed.
questions.prompt: Name this type of social engineering attack.
questions.markSchemeHint: Quid pro quo (also check baiting/phishing context, though OCR R050 specifically defines exchanging a service/benefit for access as Quid pro quo).

questions.prompt: Identify one logical prevention measure that controls the files allocated to an employee.
questions.markSchemeHint: Access rights / access permissions / user access levels.

questions.scenarioContext: A managing director wants to hold an online meeting with his managers who are based in different countries.
questions.prompt: Identify the distribution channel he could use to hold this meeting.
questions.markSchemeHint: Video conferencing / VoIP / collaboration platform (e.g., Teams/Zoom) / messaging.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Talent Show (PTS) has asked a web designer to design a website to advertise its talent shows. The web designer will follow the project life cycle and will use a mind map to plan the website.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the web designer of using a mind map to generate ideas for the PTS website.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: helps visually brainstorm and link related website sections/features quickly; easy to add/reorganise branches; clear overview to present and agree ideas with PTS before building.

questions.scenarioContext: People who want to enter Progress Talent Show (PTS) must email PTS, receive an interactive form by email, complete it, and email it back. PTS downloads the details and imports them into its database.
questions.prompt: Describe one advantage and one disadvantage to PTS of using this method to collect the data to import into its database.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): digital form data can be imported directly without retyping paper forms, reducing transcription errors and saving time; validation rules can be built into the interactive form. Disadvantage (2): multi-step email process is slow/clunky for applicants and staff; risk of attachments carrying malware/viruses or going to spam; incomplete/wrongly formatted forms may fail database import.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Talent Show (PTS) stores entrant personal details imported into its database. The web designer has recommended logical prevention measures to protect the stored entry details.
questions.prompt:
Discuss logical prevention measures that could be used.

Your response must include how the logical prevention measures will reduce the risk of a cyber security attack on the stored entry details.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 10-mark Level of Response. Detailed discussion of multiple logical prevention measures applied to PTS's database—such as Firewalls (block unauthorised network traffic/hackers), Encryption (makes stolen entrant records unreadable), Strong Passwords & 2FA (prevents unauthorised logins), Access Rights/Permissions (limits staff access to sensitive entrant data), Anti-malware/Anti-virus (scans emailed forms for Trojans/ransomware), Secure Backups & Software Updates—explaining how each reduces specific cyber risks.

questions.prompt: Identify the IT legislation that relates to employees using IT systems for long periods of time.
questions.markSchemeHint: Health and Safety at Work Act (1974) / Display Screen Equipment (DSE) Regulations.

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between data manipulation and data modification.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data modification is making authorised/general changes or updates to data (or changing stored values), whereas data manipulation in cyber-security refers to maliciously/deliberately altering or tampering with data to mislead, corrupt outcomes, or gain an unfair advantage (award 1 mark per clear contrasting definition).

questions.scenarioContext: Feedback is collected from parents and teachers after each ski trip. Paper-based questionnaires are used to gather the feedback. SP uses the feedback to create an integrated document.
questions.prompt: Other than paper-based questionnaires, identify and describe two other methods that could be used to collect feedback from parents and teachers.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks each (1 mark method + 2 marks description applied to ski trip feedback): e.g., Online survey/questionnaire (sent via link/email, auto-collates results quickly), Interviews (1-to-1 phone/in-person conversations gathering detailed qualitative opinions), Focus groups (small discussion group of parents/teachers exploring improvements together), Email feedback / Online poll / Social media poll.
